edits.new: When an Atlas API access list is required, allow the calling build host's public egress address. Obtaining a token does not prove its use is allowed: Atlas applies IP access lists to using service account access tokens, not to creating or revoking them. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access/

evidence.quote: You can generate a token from any IP address, but you can only use it to call the API (Application Programming Interface) if your IP address is on the access list.
If you make a request to the Atlas Administration API without an IP access list entry, the server responds with a 403 status code.

statements.statement: When an access list is required, allow the build host's public egress address.
statements.note: Requests must originate from listed addresses; otherwise 403.

statements.statement: Atlas applies the list to API calls rather than token creation or revocation.
statements.note: Docs note says lists apply to using tokens, not creating or revoking them.

statements.statement: Percona independently reports ORG_REQUIRES_ACCESS_LIST when its API-key workflow lacks an entry.
statements.note: Two searches found no Percona source; only a MongoDB forum thread with the error code.

edits.rationale: The Atlas docs establish that access lists apply to using tokens, not creating or revoking them, and that a request without an access list entry gets a 403. No source was found for the Percona report of ORG_REQUIRES_ACCESS_LIST, so that sentence is removed. The error code itself appears in a MongoDB community forum thread, but that thread was not pinned and does not mention Percona.

edits.old: Integration pattern inferred from the component documentation: store Atlas credentials in Google Secret Manager, authorize the Cloud Build execution service account to retrieve that secret, and use the retrieved credentials for a separate Atlas token exchange. Google IAM secret access does not itself assign Atlas administrative roles. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
edits.new: Integration pattern inferred from the component documentation (not stated as a single documented workflow): grant the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role for the secret to the service account used for the build, and use the retrieved Atlas service account client ID and client secret in a separate Atlas token request. Atlas roles are granted within Atlas by an Organization Owner, not by Google IAM. Sources: https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/securing-builds/use-secrets ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access/

evidence.quote: The client secret acts as the password when creating access tokens.
To grant a service account access to a project, you must have [`Organization Owner`]

statements.statement: Authorize the Cloud Build execution service account to retrieve the secret from Secret Manager.
statements.note: Secret Accessor role on the build service account.

statements.statement: Use the retrieved Atlas credentials for a separate Atlas token exchange.
statements.note: Atlas service account client secret is used to create access tokens; the storage-in-Secret-Manager step is the inferred combination.

statements.statement: Google IAM secret access does not itself assign Atlas administrative roles.
statements.note: Atlas roles are granted within Atlas by an Organization Owner.

edits.rationale: Google documents granting Secret Accessor to the build service account. Atlas documents that a service account's client secret acts as the password when creating access tokens, and that roles are granted in Atlas. The combined pattern is an inference; no single source documents it end to end.
